title: Six Steamed Bread
simplified_paragraphs: 一天早上，小和尚发现师父和大师兄都得到了六个馒头，而他只得到了四个馒头。小和尚觉得这太不公平了，于是他找到师父，也要了六个馒头。很快，小和尚就把六个馒头吃完了，他吃得很饱。
过了一会儿，小和尚觉得肚子胀，口也很渴，就去喝了半碗水。几分钟后，小和尚的肚子比刚才更胀了，他的肚子开始难受起来。
这时，师父对小和尚说："虽然你多得到了两个馒头，但是你并没有享受到这两个馒头的好处，相反，它们给你带来了痛苦。记住，得到不一定就是享受，知足常乐。”
traditional_paragraphs: 一天早上，小和尚發現師父和大師兄都得到了六個饅頭，而他只得到了四個饅頭。小和尚覺得這太不公平了，於是他找到師父，也要了六個饅頭。很快，小和尚就把六個饅頭吃完了，他吃得很飽。
過了一會兒，小和尚覺得肚子脹，口也很渴，就去喝了半碗水。幾分鐘後，小和尚的肚子比剛才更脹了，他的肚子開始難受起來。
這時，師父對小和尚說："雖然你多得到了兩個饅頭，但是你並沒有享受到這兩個饅頭的好處，相反，它們給你帶來了痛苦。記住，得到不一定就是享受，知足常樂。”
pinyin_paragraphs: yī tiān zǎo shang， xiǎo hé shang fā xiàn shī fu hé dà shī xiōng dōu dé dào le liù gè mán tou， ér tā zhǐ dé dào le sì gè mán tou。 xiǎo hé shang jué de zhè tài bù gōng píng le， yú shì tā zhǎo dào shī fu， yě yào le liù gè mán tou。 hěn kuài， xiǎo hé shang jiù bǎ liù gè mán tou chī wán le， tā chī de hěn bǎo。
guò le yī huì r， xiǎo hé shang jué de dù zi zhàng， kǒu yě hěn kě， jiù qù hē le bàn wǎn shuǐ。 jǐ fēn zhōng hòu， xiǎo hé shang de dù zi bǐ gāng cái gèng zhàng le， tā de dù zi kāi shǐ nán shòu qǐ lái。

zhè shí， shī fu duì xiǎo hé shang shuō：" suī rán nǐ duō dé dào le liǎng gè mán tou， dàn shì nǐ bìng méi yǒu xiǎng shòu dào zhè liǎng gè mán tou de hǎo chù， xiāng fǎn， tā men gěi nǐ dài lái le tòng kǔ。 jì zhu， dé dào bù yī dìng jiù shì xiǎng shòu， zhī zú cháng lè。”
english_paragraphs: One morning, a young monk noticed that his master and senior fellow monk had each been given six steamed buns, while he had received only four. He thought this was terribly unfair, so he went to his master and asked for six too. He quickly ate all six and felt very full.
After a while, the young monk felt bloated and thirsty, so he drank half a bowl of water. A few minutes later, his stomach felt even more bloated, and it began to hurt.

Then his master said to him, “You may have gotten two extra buns, but you didn’t enjoy them. Instead, they caused you pain. Remember, getting more doesn’t necessarily mean enjoying more. Learn to be content, and you’ll be happy.”
english_full:
One morning, a young monk noticed that his master and senior fellow monk had each been given six steamed buns, while he had received only four. He thought this was terribly unfair, so he went to his master and asked for six too. He quickly ate all six and felt very full.

After a while, the young monk felt bloated and thirsty, so he drank half a bowl of water. A few minutes later, his stomach felt even more bloated, and it began to hurt.

Then his master said to him, “You may have gotten two extra buns, but you didn’t enjoy them. Instead, they caused you pain. Remember, getting more doesn’t necessarily mean enjoying more. Learn to be content, and you’ll be happy.”
